title: Medicines
description: When you can give a child a medicine, the permission you need and the records you keep. Based on section 3 of the EYFS statutory framework.

questions.prompt: When can you give a child a medicine?

options.text: Only when the child’s parent or carer has given written permission for that particular medicine
When the child asks for it
When another member of staff says it is fine
When the child has a temperature

questions.explanation: Medicine, both prescription and non-prescription, must only be given where written permission for that particular medicine has been obtained from the child’s parent or carer.

learnMore.title: EYFS statutory framework for group and school-based providers

questions.prompt: You must keep a written record each time a medicine is given to a child. True or false?

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: True. Providers must keep a written record each time a medicine is administered, and tell the child’s parents or carers on the same day, or as soon as reasonably practicable.

learnMore.title: EYFS statutory framework for group and school-based providers

questions.prompt: When must parents or carers be told that their child has had a medicine?

options.text: On the same day, or as soon as reasonably practicable
At the end of the week
Only if the child was unwell afterwards
Only if the parent asks

questions.explanation: Parents and carers must be told on the same day the medicine has been taken, or as soon as reasonably practicable.

learnMore.title: EYFS statutory framework for group and school-based providers

questions.prompt: Written permission is only needed for prescription medicines, not for things like children’s paracetamol or teething gel. True or false?

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: False. The rule covers both prescription and non-prescription medicines. Written permission for that particular medicine is needed in both cases.

learnMore.title: EYFS statutory framework for group and school-based providers

questions.prompt: Which prescription medicines can a setting give?

options.text: Only those prescribed for that child by a doctor, dentist, nurse or pharmacist
Any prescription medicine in the building
A medicine prescribed for a brother or sister
Any medicine a parent hands over

questions.explanation: Prescription medicines must not be given unless they have been prescribed for the child by a doctor, dentist, nurse or pharmacist. Medicines containing aspirin should only be given if prescribed by a doctor.

learnMore.title: EYFS statutory framework for group and school-based providers

questions.prompt: What must happen if giving a medicine needs medical or technical knowledge?

options.text: Staff must have training first
Any member of staff can do it
The child waits until the parent arrives
The manager signs the form and nothing else is needed

questions.explanation: Staff must have training if administering the medicine requires medical or technical knowledge. The setting also needs a way to keep each child’s medicine needs up to date.

learnMore.title: EYFS statutory framework for group and school-based providers

questions.prompt: What must a setting have for children who are ill or infectious?

options.text: A procedure, discussed with parents and carers, for taking action and preventing the spread of infection
Nothing, parents decide
A rule that sick children stay all day
A notice on the door

questions.explanation: Providers must have a procedure, discussed with parents and carers, for taking appropriate action if children are ill or infectious. It must also cover the steps needed to prevent infection spreading.

learnMore.title: EYFS statutory framework for group and school-based providers

questions.prompt: A parent hands you a bottle of children’s liquid medicine at drop-off and says, “She might need a dose after lunch.” There is no form and nothing is written down.

choices.text: Tell your manager, and ask the parent to complete written permission for that medicine before it is given
choices.feedback: Right. Written permission for that particular medicine is needed before any dose, even for non-prescription medicine.

choices.text: Give a dose after lunch, as the parent asked
choices.feedback: A spoken request is not written permission.

choices.text: Give a dose and write it down afterwards
choices.feedback: The permission must be in writing before the medicine is given, not after.

questions.explanation: Medicine, including non-prescription medicine, must only be given with written permission for that particular medicine from the parent or carer. A written record must be kept each time one is given.
